primitives.name: Data Pretense Inhibition
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Integrity rule Do not pretend blocked, metadata-only, fixture-backed, license-required, or partner-required data is active.
primitives.assumptions: All data sources must be actively licensed or activated; inactive sources are not considered in active inference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a source is blocked due to rights or activation status, it is isolated into a queue.

layer2.mapping: The integrity rule maps to a Bayesian evidence filter that excludes inactive data from probabilistic inference.
layer2.telemetry: Source activation status and rights compliance metrics.

primitives.name: Active Source Activation Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Built now Rights gates, media metadata fixtures, expert activation queues, source activation ROI, King gap map, proof reports, explanation templates, decision-card contracts, owned-signal fixtures, product readiness scores, and Claude UI contracts.
primitives.assumptions: All components are built-in and operational within the system's active state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when any component is missing or non-operational.

layer2.mapping: The framework defines a kernel of active data sources and their readiness for inference.
layer2.telemetry: Product readiness score and activation ROI per source.

primitives.name: Automated Queue Isolation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Human action minimized Every blocked source is isolated into rights/activation/outreach queues with fallback source, expected next action, and product impact.
primitives.assumptions: Blocked sources are automatically isolated without manual intervention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Manual override required only in exceptional cases or system failure.

layer2.mapping: Queue isolation mirrors a state transition system where blocked sources enter a deterministic fallback path.
layer2.telemetry: Queue depth, fallback source availability, and expected next action timestamp.

The core operators define a closed-loop data sovereignty system. The integrity rule ensures that only activated data contributes to inference, preventing spurious conclusions from blocked or inactive sources. The built-now framework provides a structured set of tools for managing data lifecycle, including rights gates, activation queues, and ROI tracking. These elements form a Bayesian decision lattice where each node represents an active data source with known readiness and activation status. The human action minimization layer automates the handling of blocked sources by isolating them into queues with fallback mechanisms, ensuring continuity of inference even when some sources are unavailable. This creates a robust, self-regulating system where failure modes are predictable and managed through automated queues and state transitions.
